Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2027 16:23:00 +0000
Subject: Renewal sync and three options for term structure

Hi Maya —

Thanks again for the time last week. As we discussed, Acme’s renewal window lands mid-October and you mentioned wanting a simpler cadence across product teams (one billing date vs three). I put together three practical paths that balance price, predictability, and the operational headache of multiple invoice cutovers. I attached a short option table. Quick summary below:

1) Two-year prepay (discounted) — single invoice, easiest ops, lower unit price, limited flexibility for mid-term scale-ups.

2) Annual true-up, co-term to Oct 31 — invoice annually, true-up based on actual usage, 10% variance buffer year 1 (no penalty up to 10% above committed units), rollover credits for underuse.

3) Blended ramp (18 mo) — front-loaded credits and graduated unit pricing; staged true-ups each 6 months.

Can you confirm which direction you prefer? If Option 2 looks best I can draft SOW language for the 10% variance buffer and the year‑one true-up mechanics and loop in Finance for billing cadence.

Next steps I propose:
- You: high-level preference by EOD Friday 9/10
- Us: draft SOW + MOPs for selected option within 3 business days
- Finalize signature/DocuSign before Oct 10 to avoid overlap with current month billing

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee

Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2027 09:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Renewal sync and three options for term structure

Soojin — good framing. A few internal notes on Option 2 language for the SOW and the associated invoice cadence: 

- Variance buffer mechanics: define as "Usage Buffer" = the percent above committed units that will not trigger immediate true-up billing. Year 1 suggested at 10%, Year 2 drop to 5% to avoid long-run regressions.
- True-up window: 30 days after period end; invoice issued within 45 days.
- Rollover credits: allow up to 20% of underutilized units to carry forward but expire at renewal.

Operational asks for Sales Ops/Finance (Stephanie): can we keep annual invoices but with an optional mid-year pro forma estimate (no billing) so Acme can plan? Also — we should flag whether the buffer is chargeable at a blended rate or at list when exceeded.

If Stephanie signs off, I'll draft the SOW bullet points and send to Maya.

—Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks — operational points:

- We can support a 10% buffer for Y1 and auto-tighten to 5% in Y2. That requires explicit SOW language: "Year 1 Usage Buffer = 10%; Year 2 Usage Buffer = 5%" and a clear true-up formula.
- Billing cadence: annual invoice on Oct 31 with mid-year planning estimate (non-binding). Finance prefers not to do staged billing more than once per year for this deal size.
- If buffer is exceeded, charge at contracted per-unit rate (not list). If they scale > 30% mid-year we should trigger an amendment path (manual approval).

I'll prepare the SOW fragment and standard billing verbiage; leave the DocuSign flow to you, Soojin.

Stephanie Nguyen
